quests.hint: Able to express ideas clearly and confidently, without stumbling over words.
quests.explanation: 'An articulate speaker' is a common phrase. Articulate is also a verb — 'to articulate an idea' means to express it clearly.
quests.textToSpeak: She is an extremely ___ speaker who always explains complex ideas very clearly.
quests.correctAnswer: She is an extremely articulate speaker who always explains complex ideas very clearly.

quests.hint: Said in as few words as possible, without losing any important meaning.
quests.explanation: 'Keep it succinct' is useful workplace advice. It's a compliment, unlike 'brief,' which can sometimes suggest something's missing.
quests.textToSpeak: Please keep your answer ___ - we have limited time for each candidate today.
quests.correctAnswer: Please keep your answer succinct - we have limited time for each candidate today.

quests.hint: Valid and acceptable, following the proper rules or reasons.
quests.explanation: 'A legitimate reason' or 'a legitimate concern' are the phrases to remember. Its opposite is 'illegitimate' or, more casually, 'a poor excuse.'
quests.textToSpeak: She had a perfectly ___ reason for missing the meeting that everyone accepted.
quests.correctAnswer: She had a perfectly legitimate reason for missing the meeting that everyone accepted.

quests.hint: Focused on what actually works in practice, rather than on ideals.
quests.explanation: 'A pragmatic approach' is common in business and problem-solving. Its opposite is 'idealistic,' which focuses on principles over practicality.
quests.textToSpeak: She took a very ___ approach to the problem rather than insisting on the ideal solution.
quests.correctAnswer: She took a very pragmatic approach to the problem rather than insisting on the ideal solution.

quests.hint: Able to adapt easily and handle many different kinds of tasks well.
quests.explanation: 'A versatile team member' or 'versatile skills' are the ones you'll hear most. The noun form is 'versatility.'
quests.textToSpeak: She is an extremely ___ team member who can handle any task she is given.
quests.correctAnswer: She is an extremely versatile team member who can handle any task she is given.

quests.hint: Examining every detail extremely closely before accepting it.
quests.explanation: Scrutinise takes an 's' in British English ('scrutinize' in American English). The noun form is 'scrutiny' — 'under scrutiny.'
quests.textToSpeak: The committee will ___ every line of the report before it is officially published.
quests.correctAnswer: The committee will scrutinise every line of the report before it is officially published.

quests.hint: Open and honest, with nothing hidden from others.
quests.explanation: 'Transparent about' decisions is common in leadership contexts. The noun form is 'transparency,' a quality many workplaces claim to value.
quests.textToSpeak: Good leaders must be completely ___ about how decisions are made within their team.
quests.correctAnswer: Good leaders must be completely transparent about how decisions are made within their team.

quests.hint: Adding something extra to make an existing thing more complete.
quests.explanation: 'Supplement your studies' is a common academic phrase. As a noun, 'a supplement' can also mean a vitamin or pill, in a different context.
quests.textToSpeak: She decided to ___ her formal studies with an online course in graphic design.
quests.correctAnswer: She decided to supplement her formal studies with an online course in graphic design.

quests.hint: Taking action before a problem happens, rather than reacting afterward.
quests.explanation: 'A proactive approach' is the opposite of 'reactive.' It's a common compliment in professional feedback.
quests.textToSpeak: Rather than waiting for issues to arise, she took a ___ approach to risk management.
quests.correctAnswer: Rather than waiting for issues to arise, she took a proactive approach to risk management.

quests.hint: A standard used to measure and compare performance against.
quests.explanation: 'Set a benchmark' or 'use as a benchmark' both sound natural here. It originally referred to a fixed reference point for measurement.
quests.textToSpeak: They used the best-performing company in the sector as their ___ for success.
quests.correctAnswer: They used the best-performing company in the sector as their benchmark for success.

quests.hint: One specific standard used to judge or decide something.
quests.explanation: Criterion is singular; its plural is 'criteria' — a common mistake is using 'criteria' for just one standard.
quests.textToSpeak: The most important ___ for selecting the winning project was real-world impact.
quests.correctAnswer: The most important criterion for selecting the winning project was real-world impact.

quests.hint: Publicly supporting and speaking up for a cause.
quests.explanation: 'Advocate for' something is the phrase to remember. As a noun, 'an advocate' is the person doing the supporting.
quests.textToSpeak: She has spent her career ___ for greater equality in access to quality education.
quests.correctAnswer: She has spent her career advocating for greater equality in access to quality education.

quests.hint: Officially setting aside a certain amount of money or resources for a purpose.
quests.explanation: 'Allocate funding' or 'allocate resources' are common phrases in budgeting and planning. The noun form is 'allocation.'
quests.textToSpeak: The government plans to ___ more funding to mental health services next year.
quests.correctAnswer: The government plans to allocate more funding to mental health services next year.

quests.hint: General agreement reached by a whole group after discussion.
quests.explanation: 'Reach a consensus' is the phrase to remember for agreeing as a group. 'General consensus' adds a touch of emphasis.
quests.textToSpeak: After hours of discussion, the team finally reached a ___ on the best way forward.
quests.correctAnswer: After hours of discussion, the team finally reached a consensus on the best way forward.

quests.hint: A difference between two things that should actually match.
quests.explanation: 'A significant discrepancy' is a common phrase, especially in reports or accounts. The plural is 'discrepancies.'
quests.textToSpeak: The auditor found a significant ___ between the reported and the actual figures.
quests.correctAnswer: The auditor found a significant discrepancy between the reported and the actual figures.

quests.hint: Existing as an idea rather than as something you can touch or see.
quests.explanation: 'A highly abstract concept' is the opposite of 'concrete.' As a noun, 'an abstract' also means a short summary of an academic paper.
quests.textToSpeak: Freedom is a highly ___ concept that different people understand very differently.
quests.correctAnswer: Freedom is a highly abstract concept that different people understand very differently.

quests.hint: An educated guess that hasn't yet been proven, used as a starting point for research.
quests.explanation: 'Test a hypothesis' is standard in scientific writing. The plural is 'hypotheses' — an irregular Greek-origin plural.
quests.textToSpeak: The researchers tested their ___ by conducting a series of carefully controlled experiments.
quests.correctAnswer: The researchers tested their hypothesis by conducting a series of carefully controlled experiments.

quests.hint: A relationship where two things tend to change together.
quests.explanation: 'A correlation between' two things is how most speakers say it. Correlation alone doesn't prove that one thing causes the other.
quests.textToSpeak: There is a well-established ___ between regular exercise and improved mental health.
quests.correctAnswer: There is a well-established correlation between regular exercise and improved mental health.

quests.hint: A conclusion reached through reasoning, based on evidence rather than being stated directly.
quests.explanation: 'Draw an inference' is the natural choice here. The verb form is 'infer' — 'we can infer that she was upset.'
quests.textToSpeak: From her response, we can draw a clear ___ that she was not happy with the decision.
quests.correctAnswer: From her response, we can draw a clear inference that she was not happy with the decision.

quests.hint: The relationship where one thing actually causes another to happen.
quests.explanation: 'Prove causation' is a phrase you'll hear in research and science. It differs from 'correlation,' where two things are simply linked.
quests.textToSpeak: The study was designed to prove ___, not just show that two factors are related.
quests.correctAnswer: The study was designed to prove causation, not just show that two factors are related.

quests.hint: The ability to understand and share how someone else is feeling.
quests.explanation: 'Show empathy toward' someone is the version people actually use. 'Empathetic' is the adjective form describing the person.
quests.textToSpeak: Good leaders show genuine ___ toward their team members during difficult times.
quests.correctAnswer: Good leaders show genuine empathy toward their team members during difficult times.

quests.hint: Considering the whole picture, not just one isolated part.
quests.explanation: 'A holistic approach' considers everything together, like body and mind. It's often contrasted with a narrower, more specialised focus.
quests.textToSpeak: The doctors took a ___ approach to her treatment, addressing both body and mind.
quests.correctAnswer: The doctors took a holistic approach to her treatment, addressing both body and mind.

quests.hint: Whether something is actually realistic and possible to carry out.
quests.explanation: 'A feasibility study' checks whether a plan will actually work before money is committed. The adjective form is 'feasible.'
quests.textToSpeak: A full ___ study was conducted before the board committed funding to the project.
quests.correctAnswer: A full feasibility study was conducted before the board committed funding to the project.

quests.hint: Everyone with a genuine interest in the outcome of a decision or project.
quests.explanation: 'Consult stakeholders' is common workplace language. It includes anyone affected — employees, customers, investors, and more.
quests.textToSpeak: All key ___ were consulted before the final plan was presented to the board.
quests.correctAnswer: All key stakeholders were consulted before the final plan was presented to the board.

quests.hint: Making a risk or problem less severe, even if you can't remove it completely.
quests.explanation: 'Mitigate the risks' is common in planning and business. It's a more formal alternative to simply 'reduce.'
quests.textToSpeak: Better planning at the start would have helped to ___ the risks significantly.
quests.correctAnswer: Better planning at the start would have helped to mitigate the risks significantly.

quests.hint: Something that triggers a big change, without necessarily being changed itself.
quests.explanation: 'Act as a catalyst for' something is the one to remember. It comes from chemistry, describing a substance that speeds up a reaction.
quests.textToSpeak: The crisis acted as a ___ for sweeping and long-overdue reforms across the system.
quests.correctAnswer: The crisis acted as a catalyst for sweeping and long-overdue reforms across the system.

quests.hint: No longer useful because something newer has replaced it.
quests.explanation: 'Become obsolete' is the standard phrase, especially common when discussing outdated technology or skills.
quests.textToSpeak: Many traditional manufacturing skills have become ___ in the age of automation.
quests.correctAnswer: Many traditional manufacturing skills have become obsolete in the age of automation.

quests.hint: No longer needed, especially describing a job role that's been cut.
quests.explanation: 'Become redundant' is common British workplace language for losing a job due to restructuring, not poor performance.
quests.textToSpeak: After the merger, many positions became ___ and the workforce had to be reduced.
quests.correctAnswer: After the merger, many positions became redundant and the workforce had to be reduced.

quests.hint: Having genuinely mixed feelings, unable to decide how you feel about something.
quests.explanation: 'Ambivalent about' something is what you'll hear most often. It differs from simply being 'indecisive' — the mixed feelings themselves are the point.
quests.textToSpeak: She felt deeply ___ about leaving the company she had worked at for twelve years.
quests.correctAnswer: She felt deeply ambivalent about leaving the company she had worked at for twelve years.

quests.hint: A person's natural tendency or temperament.
quests.explanation: 'A sunny disposition' is a lovely idiom for a naturally cheerful personality. 'Disposition toward' shows what someone naturally leans toward.
quests.textToSpeak: She has a natural ___ toward optimism that makes her an inspiring person to be around.
quests.correctAnswer: She has a natural disposition toward optimism that makes her an inspiring person to be around.
